title: An image model labels hybrid nerve-tumor slides in a small held-out set
summary: A retrospective study of 115 nerve-sheath tumors compared image classifiers for hybrid neurofibroma/schwannoma and related diagnoses. In 17 held-out hybrid-only slides from another center/scanner, the best reported model reached mean accuracy 0.96. This selected positive-class test does not establish specificity against other tumors or clinical utility.
ai_technology: ResNet50 features and clustering-constrained attention multiple instance learning
organization: University of Augsburg; University Hospital Hamburg-Eppendorf

source_review.scope: Primary full-text bibliographic dates, computational classification Methods, held-out Results and explicit cohort/reference limitations.

evidence.tested: The 115 tumors supplied 375 histological sections across three German centers. Authors report patient-separated cross-validation; a 17-slide hybrid-only holdout assessed scanner/center transfer. The reported best mCLAM/ResNet50 configuration with stain normalization achieved accuracy 0.96 ± 0.05 and F1 0.98 ± 0.03.
evidence.unknown: The holdout contains only hybrid-tumor slides, so it does not measure external three-class specificity. Its distinct patient count is not clear from the main text. Different configurations were compared on the test set, and best test performance is not a locked-model estimate. Expert-curated referral cases, artifacts and center/scanner confounding limit generalization; prospective clinical outcomes were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Learned image features and multiple-instance classifiers predicted diagnostic slide labels; expert histology supplied reference diagnoses.
